headline: Semis fell 3.0% and the Nasdaq is in correction as Nvidia's leadership limbo meets a 5.15% 10-year, heading into a week with Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's IPO, while cooling rose 6.2% against the tide.
regime: Risk-off in hardware, risk-on in physical infrastructure: Semis ETF -3.0% on the day and -13.8% on the month, compute -5.0%, networking -5.1%, while cooling +6.2% (+23.8% on five days) and power/grid fell only 1-1.5%. The 10-year rose to 5.15% (+6.1% on five days), PPI is running 6.5% and Bitcoin is -12.8% on the week, so leverage is unwinding. The market is rewarding the bottleneck owners with cash flow and punishing debt-funded capacity and the Nvidia complex.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Cooling +6.2% on a day semis fell 3%; MOD +40.4% and CEG +12.1% on five days (digest segments)
Analysts frame power and cooling as where AI spend is flowing (94ebde59ea44, 9249b27235b3)
Against: Vistra booked a $269m impairment (ca64b95899a7); Bloom at 39x forward earnings (968554188d78); Cameco's CEO says AI isn't the reason to own nuclear (5b96df9745ca)
theses.change_note: +2: the bottleneck segments held up in a broad AI selloff, which is the relative-strength test the thesis needs; Vistra's impairment keeps it from rising more.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Michael Dell: H100 rents up 58% in a year to $3.10/hour; CoreWeave says older-GPU prices are rising (bdd89b8e2ef1)
AMD: 'demand is higher than supply' after an Oppenheimer upgrade (e9643687f32d)
Marvell is paying $115bn for Lumentum to own optical capacity (5db6a6a5e9eb)
Against: Chanos notes Nebius's 2027 guide is flat at $8-9m per MW (83f63cdb9822); Semis ETF -13.8% on the month
theses.change_note: +3: rising rental prices for three-year-old GPUs are hard evidence of scarcity and rebut the depreciation bear case.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Nebius slashed its revenue outlook and analysts keep cutting targets (6530a07cc0f9, f6ad2e9c5c46); flat revenue per MW (83f63cdb9822)
IREN -63% in a year on debt-funded build-out worries (695d157207c9); KBW flags Bitdeer's export-control exposure (6563eb971d2b)
Segment -4.3% on the day; all neoclouds fail the quality gate (shortlist)
Against: CORZ +23.5% on five days; bullish CoreWeave calls (481cb73e293d)
theses.change_note: +1: more target cuts and Chanos's unit-economics critique; the CORZ bounce is a counterpoint but not about credit.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: DRAM now costs more than AI memory as HBM eats wafer capacity (3f9385969425); Micron expanded its buyback (ecb7e55a7235)
WDC at 7.3x forward earnings with a 41% operating margin (shortlist); memory +11.4% on five days
Against: -4.0% on the day and -24.1% on the month; WDC on short sellers' worst list after a 17% drop (88f6b5a987d7); DRAM price-fixing suit survives dismissal (42e7d480c58d)
theses.change_note: Pricing evidence improved but the segment gave back 4% and the lawsuit adds a new tail; net flat.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Oracle fails the cash-flow quality gate (shortlist)
Prior: Oracle's backlog is about half OpenAI; Alphabet borrowing to fund AI (2026-11-13 worldview)
Against: hyperscalers +0.1% on the day, the steadiest AI segment; Microsoft shrugged off a global outage (f74c2d71718b); a federal 'national champions' plan would favour them (f04a0d1c458d)
theses.change_note: -2: Monday check: today's digest alone gives no new evidence for this; it survives on carry-forward while the tape treats hyperscalers as the safe haven.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: 10-year 5.15%, +6.1% on five days; PPI 6.5% (digest tape, d9f7afa65a5e); Deutsche Bank warns rate-hike risk is underpriced (4c4285b37a7d)
Nasdaq in correction (4dbf2b10d1ae); Bitcoin -12.8% on the week (bfe1b0303333); investors scrambling to measure AI exposure (0dbf1e5110ce)
Against: Morgan Stanley says go 'max' overweight stocks (77c5090f2254)
theses.change_note: +2: yields and inflation kept rising and the Nasdaq crossed into correction; one bullish strategist doesn't offset the tape.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: State elections are shifting where AI investment goes (68c1ffb74ed5); Washington is tightening chip exports (9249b27235b3)
Against: the administration plans AI 'national champions' including Nvidia, Amazon and Microsoft (f04a0d1c458d); grid and power outperformed today
theses.change_note: -3: Monday check: only thin support in today's digest, and federal policy is leaning pro-AI; largely survives on carry-forward.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: Huang reportedly considering a return; the board faces a 'Huang problem' before earnings this week (c2c274adb878, 6936074d2869)
NVDA -12.8% on five days vs AMD +18.9%; compute -5.0% on the day (digest segments)
Tighter GPU export controls are being priced into Bitdeer and others (6563eb971d2b)
Against: median target $280, well above the price (91503a17348d)
theses.change_note: The leadership question is now open in both directions and earnings will decide; no reason to move until then.

compute.note: -5.0% on the day; AMD gains what NVDA loses, Nvidia earnings this week.

foundry_equipment.note: +10.2% on five days but -17.6% on the month; export risk hangs over it.

memory_storage.note: DRAM pricing strong and WDC at 7.3x, but -24.1% on the month.

networking_optical.note: Marvell-Lumentum shows strategic value; -5.1% on the day.

servers.note: -23.9% on the month, thin margins; SMCI on short sellers' list.

power_nuclear.note: CEG +12.1% on five days; Vistra impairment is the warning.

grid_electrical.note: Only -1.1% in a hard tape; PWR +11.3% on five days.

cooling_thermal.note: +6.2% on the day, +23.8% on five; MOD +40.4%.

datacenter_neocloud.note: -4.3% on the day; Nebius guide cut, IREN -63% in a year.

hyperscalers.note: Flat on the day; the market's safe haven within AI.

ai_software.note: -19.4% on the month; AI search hitting traffic plays like Reddit.

risks: Nvidia earnings this week under an interim CEO could reset the whole compute and server complex.
The 10-year at 5.15% with 6.5% PPI makes a Fed hike live, hitting every long-duration AI name.
Tighter China export controls would hit compute, equipment and neocloud expansions together.
Neocloud financing stress could spill into supplier order books.
An Anthropic IPO stumble would dent the private-market AI valuations underpinning capex.
watch: Nvidia's earnings and any decision on Huang's return.
Anthropic's IPO pricing and first-day trade.
10-year vs 5.15% and Fed Chair Warsh's lean on hikes.
Whether cooling holds its +23.8% five-day run or reverses.
Sandisk's 8-for-1 split on Nov 19 and memory's reaction.
